bibl.title: Ancient Armenian Corpus, Parts of Speech Tagset, May 2021
bibl.note: Source supplied by Lewis Read as GREGORI TAG set.pdf. All 35 listed codes are preserved. No later version or additional GREgORI morphological specification is assumed.

projectDesc.p: This file documents the two linguistic annotation fields used on corpus word tokens: the exact GREgORI POS code in w/@pos and the project's compact morphological description in w/@msd. Words use these values directly; they do not require repeated authority pointers to their POS or morphological definitions. Lemma identity is handled separately in lemmata.xml.

GREgORI's May 2021 POS inventory is preserved below. MSD categories document all seven Classical Armenian cases, singular and plural, and verbal form, tense or stem, mood, voice, and person. The MSD notation is a project convention supplementing GREgORI, not an extension attributed to the GREgORI source sheet or a claim of full Universal Dependencies annotation.

editorialDecl.p: Use w/@lemma for the adopted headword, w/@lemmaRef for its lexical entry, w/@pos for the exact GREgORI code, and w/@msd for contextual morphology. Where lemmaRef is supplied, lemma must match the referenced headword. POS and MSD values need no additional authority pointers. Preserve the text's editorial markup.

MSD values are case-sensitive, separated by dots without spaces or feature prefixes. Nominal order is case.number, for example Nom.Pl. Finite verbal order is tense-or-stem.mood.voice.person.number, for example Aor.Ind.Pass.3.Sg. Omit inapplicable or unestablished features, retaining the order of those recorded: Pres.Ind.3.Sg, Imp.2.Pl, and 3.Sg are permitted. Record pending or ambiguous analysis separately; do not combine competing values with slashes or commas.

Case codes are Nom, Gen, Dat, Acc, Abl, Ins, and Loc; number is Sg or Pl; grammatical person is 1, 2, or 3. Determine case from the construction, including where forms coincide; address does not introduce a separate vocative case. Finite verbs receive no case. MSD person and number must agree with any values already specified by the GREgORI pronoun code.

Finite verbs retain pos="V". Pres, Aor, and Impf identify present, aorist, and imperfect forms; Ind, Sub, Imp, and Proh identify indicative, subjunctive, imperative, and prohibitive. In Pres.Sub and Aor.Sub, the first code identifies the stem formation, not present or past temporal meaning. Voice is Act or Pass, with Pass covering the mediopassive; record it only where morphologically established.

Non-finite verbal forms also retain pos="V". Use Inf for an infinitive, Part for a participle, Vnoun for a declinable verbal noun, and Conv for the non-finite -ոց form used in necessitive/future constructions. Their order is form.voice.case.number, with only applicable, established features supplied: Inf, Part.Gen.Pl, or Vnoun.Gen.Sg. Non-finite forms receive no grammatical person.

taxonomy.desc: Exact source codes and meanings from the supplied May 2021 sheet; internal IDs provide stable project references.

category.catDesc: If it is impossible to analyze a form, this form itself is chosen as lemma, called a lemma-form.

taxonomy.n: Project MSD: nominal and verbal morphology
taxonomy.desc: Project morphology vocabulary used directly in w/@msd. Nominal order: case.number. Finite verbal order: tense-or-stem.mood.voice.person.number. Non-finite order: form.voice.case.number. Use only applicable, established features and retain their relative order. These definitions supplement GREgORI; they are not GREgORI POS codes.

category.catDesc: Grammatical case of the contextual form: Nom, Gen, Dat, Acc, Abl, Ins, or Loc.
Nominative. Base case; commonly the subject form and also used in address.
Genitive. Genitive; distinguish from dative by contextual analysis where forms coincide.
Dative. Dative; commonly marks recipients and other context-dependent relations.
Accusative. Accusative; commonly marks direct objects, with or without the appropriate particle.
Ablative. Ablative; includes source or separation constructions.
Instrumental. Instrumental; includes means, instrument, and other supported uses.
Locative. Locative; includes location in space or time, assessed from its construction.
Grammatical number of the contextual form: Sg or Pl.
Grammatical person of finite verbs; not assigned to non-finite forms.
The same slot identifies indicative tense or subjunctive stem formation; it does not always indicate temporal meaning.
Present indicative, or present-stem formation with Sub.
Aorist indicative, or aorist-stem formation with Sub.
Imperfect indicative. Distinct from Imp, the imperative mood code.
Finite verbal mood. Imperative and prohibitive normally omit the tense-or-stem slot.
Subjunctive; may express future, wish, or other contextual modal meanings. Combine with Pres or Aor to distinguish stem formations.
Prohibitive: the verb form in a negative command. The negative particle is tagged separately; not every negated verb is prohibitive.
Morphologically established voice; omit for forms that do not distinguish it. These values do not encode causative derivation.
Mediopassive morphology, including passive, middle, or reflexive uses. Do not determine the code solely from the English translation.
Non-finite forms retain GREgORI pos="V"; finite status is indicated by a finite mood rather than a redundant Fin prefix.
Infinitive used as a non-finite verbal complement; no person or automatically assigned case.
Participle, normally the Classical Armenian past participle. Record case and number where established by the construction, including attributive and predicative uses.
Declinable verbal noun, traditionally also described as an inflected infinitive. Use Vnoun.Gen.Sg rather than Inf.Gen.Sg for this adopted distinction.
Indeclinable non-finite form in -ոց used with the copula in necessitive/future constructions. Conv is the project code adopted from the UD description; no case or person is assigned.

body.p: GREgORI POS and project MSD definitions are both recorded as categories in encodingDesc/classDecl. Words use the documented codes directly; no per-word references to these category definitions are required.
